issues.description: Function name/signature mismatch: the header declares check_sphere_hit(...) but the implementation and callers use ray_sphere_intersect(...). This inconsistency between declaration, definition and usage will cause compilation errors (missing prototype in C++ and/or link errors) and confuses students about the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the declaration and definition: change the header to declare 'bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius);' (or rename the implementation and all callers to 'check_sphere_hit' consistently). Ensure the header, implementation and all call sites use the exact same function name and signature.

issues.description: The sphere-intersection function is referenced with different identifiers across artifacts: the template header declares check_sphere_hit(...) while the template implementation and the solution use ray_sphere_intersect(...). This breaks the conceptual mapping (and in C++ will cause a missing prototype / compile-time mismatch) — students reading the header will expect check_sphere_hit but the rest of the code and the solution target ray_sphere_intersect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent: change the template header declaration to 'bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius);' (matching the implementation and the solution), or alternatively rename the implementation and solution to 'check_sphere_hit' everywhere. Prefer aligning the template header with the existing implementation name 'ray_sphere_intersect' to avoid breaking compilation and reduce student confusion.
